report.source_text: A routine follow-up CT scan after 6 months showed multiple (approximately 20 in number) new nodules up to 2 cm in size, scattered in both lungs with a lower lobar predominance (Fig. 1). An enhancing soft tissue nodule measuring 2 cm in size was seen at the right T4–5 intervertebral foramen (Fig. 2). There was erosion of the adjacent lamina and pedicle. This nodule was protruding into the spinal canal without any significant mass effect on the spinal cord. There was no associated lymphadenopathy in chest or abdomen.

report.source_text: Because a metastatic process was the primary concern, a thoracoscopic wedge excision of two of the peripheral lung nodules from different lobes was performed. On microscopy, an admixture of lymphocytes, plasma cells and eosinophils were seen in the affected lung tissue. Focal areas of fibrosis were present in areas of inflamed lung (Fig. 3). Gram, fungal and acid fast stains were negative for microorganisms (not shown). The possibility of inflammatory pseudotumor was considered on the initial pathology report, but considering the absence of abundant myofibroblasts, a final pathologic diagnosis of chronic pneumonitis was given.

report.source_text: No treatment was offered, and follow-up CT performed after 18 months showed resolution of the lung nodules (not shown). The intervertebral foramen lesion had also resolved, leaving behind only the persistent bony defect (Fig. 4).

clinician.trajectory_summary: An asymptomatic 70-year-old male with a history of resected dermal sarcoma presented with multiple new pulmonary nodules and an enhancing soft tissue nodule at the T4-5 intervertebral foramen on routine follow-up CT. A thoracoscopic wedge excision of lung nodules revealed chronic pneumonitis with an admixture of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and eosinophils, and focal fibrosis; Gram, fungal, and acid-fast stains were negative. Inflammatory pseudotumor was considered but not definitively diagnosed pathologically due to the absence of abundant myofibroblasts. Given the multiple lung nodules and the intervertebral mass, the final clinical and radiological impression was an inflammatory process resembling an inflammatory pseudotumor. No treatment was offered, and follow-up CT after 18 months showed complete resolution of both the lung nodules and the intervertebral foramen lesion.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial CT scan revealed multiple new pulmonary nodules and an enhancing soft tissue nodule at the right T4-5 intervertebral foramen with bone erosion.
Thoracoscopic wedge excision of lung nodules showed chronic pneumonitis with an inflammatory infiltrate (lymphocytes, plasma cells, eosinophils) and fibrosis; infectious causes were ruled out.
The final clinical and radiological impression was an inflammatory process resembling an inflammatory pseudotumor, considering the widespread nature of the lesions.
Both pulmonary and intervertebral lesions resolved spontaneously without treatment after 18 months, supporting an inflammatory etiology.
